question.text: A trapezium is formed by the pair of tangents of parabola <math><mi>P</mi><mi></mi><mo>:</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math> drawn from the centre of the ellipse <math><mi>E</mi><mi></mi><mo>:</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac></math>, tangent at the vertex of <math><mi>P</mi></math> and the tangent at end point of the minor axis of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>E</mi></math>. The area (in sq. units) of the trapezium is

solution.text:
The equation of the tangents from the centre of the ellipse to the parabola are y=±x

The equation of the tangent at the vertex P of the parabola is y=1

The equation of the tangent at the end point of the minor axis of the ellipse is y=12

 Hence, the area of trapezium ABCD = 1 2 ⋅ 1 2 1+2 = 3 4  sq. units
